description:
Read one clip: elements (canvas px), voiceover (text, voice, duration, voiceover_volume), background, transition (null if none). Three independent axes:
- `select` shapes the JSON. Full reads are large (word timings and type_data dominate); ask only for what you need.
- `element_ids` picks which element rows (e.g. element_ids: ['el_9'], select: ['elements.x','elements.y']).
- `render` returns a PNG; omit it and nothing renders.

render cheat sheet:
  {}                                  → t=0 (entry animations not yet in: check several mid-clip moments instead)
  {timestamps: [0.5, 2, 4]}           → one labelled grid (~¼ the tokens of separate frames)
  {element_id: 'e1'}                  → that animation cropped, four moments
  {element_id: 'e1', test: {cues: {land: 1.2}}} → with other values/timeline, nothing saved
  {preview: '<token>'}                → an edit_animation dry run, cropped (a site placed nowhere here: alone on the clip)
  {filmstrip: true}                   → whole clip as 12 frames + a timeline of cues, actions, element starts/ends
  {save: true}                        → also returns presigned_url
  select: [] + render: {}             → the PNG alone (default for one animation)
A render of one animation also returns { warnings } (glow cut at its box, text off its frame, frames near the limits).

Elements: id, element_type, name, x, y, width, height, start_time, end_time, rotation + type data (textdata/shapedata/imagedata/videodata/zoomdata/…) + `keyframes` in add_elements' wire shape (round-trips into update_elements). An HTML animation (codedata.version 2) carries `html_mograph`: status + the parameters, actions and cues its page declares (the vocabulary for update_elements param_tracks/actions/cues, e.g. update_elements({updates:[{element_id, type_data:{cues:[{op:'set', key, wordIndex, offset}]}}]})); files via read_animation. An older canvas animation carries `animation`; it plays and exports as is.

element_ids.description: Which element rows to return ([] = none). Writes already echo resolved layout, so re-reads are often unnecessary.

render.description: Render a PNG (present = render; `{}` = t=0). Checking work: several mid-clip `timestamps`, not t=0: text and images have ~0.4s entry animations so a correct edit looks empty at t=0 while shapes show. Or `animations: false`.

animations.description: Default true (the frame as the video shows it). false: every element settled at its final position and opacity: check COMPOSITION without mid-flight elements looking misplaced.

element_id.description: Only this element over the background, cropped to its box, one small sheet (an HTML animation is drawn from its page, own values and timeline). No timestamps → four moments.

around.description: Center the window on a cue ('cue:land') or an action clip ('action:hop', by name or id) instead of from/to. On a whole clip, a cue several animations share is 'cue:land@<element name>'.

fps.description: Frames per second instead of a count, e.g. 8 over 2 s is 17, capped at 16.

frames.description: How many frames across the window, first and last included (default 12, max 16).

from.description: Window start, element-local seconds, or clip seconds for a whole clip (default 0).

seam.description: get_clip of a whole clip only: the cut from this clip into the next, as the player shows it: this clip's last second, its transition, and the next clip's first second, in this clip's seconds; takes frames, no window. Every cut of the film at once: get_project({render: {seams: true}}).

span.description: With around: the window's length in seconds (default 2 around a cue; the clip plus 0.5 around an action).

to.description: Window end, element-local seconds, or clip seconds for a whole clip (default the end).

filmstrip.description: Motion in ONE image: evenly spaced labelled frames (default 12 over the whole animation) with a timeline of cues (lines) and action clips (bars): judge pacing, easing, beats on cues. true, or {from, to} / {around, span}, with frames or fps. Replaces timestamps. get_clip without element_id/preview: the whole clip in clip seconds, ticks for each element's start/end. HTML animations are drawn from their pages, the next clip's across a seam included.

layout.description: Several timestamps: 'sheet' (default, one image) | 'separate' (full-size, ~4x tokens; only when a cell is too small).

max_width.description: Returned image width: default 960 (frame), 1280 (whole grid). ~(w×h)/750 tokens; raise only for small print. One animation: the resolution drawn before the crop (sheet cells stay ≤360px; closer → layout:'separate' or a clip frame).

preview.description: Token from edit_animation(dry_run: true): the unsaved page drawn and cropped like element_id (its element, else one using that site, else the page alone on this clip). Nothing saved.

save.description: Also upload the image and return presigned_url (→ update_clueprint files=[{path, source_url}]). One image: not with layout:'separate'.

test.description: Try other settings on the one animation rendered (element_id or preview), nothing saved; element-local (page) seconds. Check a value or cue before setting it with update_elements.

actions.description: Action clips to try instead of the element's: [{name, start, duration?, args?}].

param_tracks.description: Keyframes to try for animatable parameters: {key: [{t, value, interpolation?}]}.

parameter_values.description: Values to try, over the element's own (an image or video value: a URL or upload).

timestamps.description: Clip seconds (default 0). Several → one labelled grid (~¼ the tokens); prefer several when checking. A cell is ⅓ width: small print → one number. Max 15; deduped, sorted.

video.description: For people: a low-res MP4 of the same window (filmstrip's, else first 10 s) as video_url (1 h link). You can't watch it: judge from the filmstrip.

select.description: JSON to return. Omit = everything; [] = clip fields only (clip_id, duration, background, voiceover_text). Sections (each returns its own key): 'elements' (whole rows); 'voiceover_words' ({word, start, end, punctuated_word}, SECONDS; null without transcription); 'groups' (id, name, parent_id, bounds_px, anchor_px, keyframes; ids for update_groups); 'busy' ([{entity_path, job_type}] still writing: EMPTY = voiceover/AI image landed; non-empty = don't write those yet). 'elements.<key>' keeps just those keys (id always): name, element_type, x, y, width, height, start_time, end_time, rotation, keyframes, textdata, shapedata, imagedata, videodata, zoomdata, codedata, clickaction, questiondata, resultsdata, formdata, avatardata, parent_id, dropShadows, animation; mixed with 'elements' → whole rows. y_top (centre-aligned text only) = the TOP edge; send it back as y with y_anchor:'top'. E.g. ['elements.x','elements.y','elements.width','elements.height'] geometry; ['elements.name','elements.start_time','elements.end_time'] timing; ['elements.textdata','voiceover_words'] copy vs VO.
